posts.excerpt: The principle "Work smarter, not harder!" apparently also applies to controlling quantum materials with light. posts.title: Mitigating the ecological consequences of light pollution
posts.excerpt: Light pollution is one of the fastest-growing and least-regulated environmental changes worldwide. posts.title: Molecular imaging reveals how shape-shifting protein complex captures DNA and holds separate sections together
posts.excerpt: Researchers at Kanazawa University and the National Institute of Genetics in Japan have used high-speed atomic force microscopy to observe how a group of proteins known as Smc5/6 interacts with DNA. The images reveal how this structure opens and closes, captures DNA and brings separate sections together. The researchers also observed Smc5/6 holding twisted sections of DNA in place, producing more tightly packed arrangements. The findings, published in Nature Communications,  provide new insights into the molecular processes that contribute to the maintenance and repair of genetic material.

posts.title: Satellite analysis finds little evidence that data centers cause widespread ground warming
posts.excerpt: A new study published in Environmental Research Letters has found little evidence that hyperscale data centers cause significant heating of surrounding land. posts.excerpt: For six decades, wildlife researchers have faced a persistent challenge: to attach a tracking device to study a wild animal, they first have to catch it. posts.title: North Atlantic's 'cold blob' may contain climate nuance

posts.title: Physicists step closer to the 'Zeptoverse' after 42-year particle search
posts.excerpt: Physicists have found evidence of a particle decay so rare that it is expected to occur only around once in every 10 billion "beauty" particles. The result, from the upgraded LHCb experiment at CERN's Large Hadron Collider (LHC), follows a search spanning more than 40 years and brings physicists closer to exploring the "Zeptoverse"—an unexplored world that exists at distances of a billionth of a trillionth of a meter, or a "zeptometer," where new particles and forces of nature may be hiding.

posts.title: A perfect weekend in the Darent valley, Kent: a ‘demi-paradise’ of art, lavender fields and great pubs
posts.excerpt: Just an hour from London, this idyllic area, beloved by painters and poets, is brimming with history, beautiful walks and fab places to eat and drink  In the 1820s, a young painter left London to live in Shoreham in the west of Kent. In his waterside cottage, Samuel Palmer – remembered now as a key figure of British Romanticism – depicted moonlit cornfields, apple trees bowed under fruit and hills swollen with light. He dubbed the area his Valley of Vision. Two centuries on, Palmer’s own vision of Shoreham – and the surrounding Darent Valley – as a demi-paradise isn’t too far from the canvas.

posts.title: 2026 Full Moon calendar: When to see the Full Moon and phases
posts.excerpt:
